title: Debate, Reconnaissance, and Resolve Before Kasur

blocks.text: As the Khalsa nears Kasur, the imbalance in numbers sharpens argument inside the camp. The timid imagine disaster while the resolute insist that the Panth must either prevail or die honorably rather than retreat from a righteous cause.

Into this debate comes timely intelligence: A Sikh traveler from Kasur happened to pass by them, and the chiefs immediately draw him into council. He becomes the means by which rumor is replaced with actionable knowledge about Kasur's gates, habits, and weak points.

The page therefore holds together two kinds of preparation at once. Moral courage is tested in open discussion while reconnaissance quietly prepares the method by which the city can actually be entered.
